The Iron Jackals.name: The Iron Jackals
The Iron Jackals.basicInfo:
The Iron Jackals — Dustfall.

A territorial salvage gang and neighborhood protection crew based in Vossan Yard.

Public work:

- Salvage processing.
- Scrap auctions.
- Heavy hauling.
- Neighborhood protection.

Criminal work:

- Protection payments.
- Stolen-component fencing.
- Cargo intimidation.
- Selective theft.

The Jackals are embedded residents rather than outside raiders. Their protection is real. So are their debts.

No organization here rules Dustfall.

Leader: Kaedra Vossan, head of the Iron Jackals and Vossan Yard. Reputation: Dustfall pays them, calls them when a transient crew threatens children, and hates the invoice.
The Iron Jackals.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The yard's protection is real and its ledger is not one book. Ralven Nox keeps a clean ledger that proves what was purchased and a second column recording what the gang actually moved, and decides nightly how much of the second Kaedra Vossan sees; some items sold at the Jackal Auction Rail came from the streets the Jackals charge to protect.

Internal split: Kaedra holds that the yard protects the streets it charges and nothing else, and that children, medicine and housing are never priced; Ralven prices everything and calculates how far she can threaten before it stops paying; Orenik Sol refuses jobs and pays for it inside the gang; Messa Taar quietly returns goods she believes should never have been taken; Jessa Quorin's early warnings come from Bent Halo trades more often than from the Rooftop Lookout Walk.

In play: The protection payment Ralven's ledger says Della Vossik and Mira Vossik owe after the Jackals kept a transient crew off the Vossik salvage crew, seated by Sennra Sol at the Dispute Table of The Long Shot (quest "Dustfall — The Yard Protection Debt"); and Cavren Zelvaris, one incident from forcing the auction question open.

A player can: argue the debt at the Dispute Table and be remembered by Ralven as someone who cost the yard money; buy a component off the Jackal Auction Rail and carry its provenance into Refit Row, where Halvora Orvantis will read it; or bring Kaedra proof of what Messa returns, which ends a kindness to save a gang.

The Bent Halo.name: The Bent Halo
The Bent Halo.basicInfo:
The Bent Halo — Dustfall.

A smuggling and extraction crew based at the Crooked Landing.

The Bent Halo moves:

- Refugees.
- Medicine.
- Restricted cargo.
- Information.
- People who cannot use official gates or roads.

The crew's humanitarian work does not erase its criminal contracts, false manifests, or selective loyalties.

No organization here rules Dustfall.

Leader: Saevik Ruun, crew chief of the Bent Halo. Reputation: useful, untrustworthy and too connected to remove; half the settlement's lanes run through the Crooked Landing.
The Bent Halo.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The cargo veto belongs to Brannoc Kest, not Saevik Ruun, and Brannoc's counts have carried people who were on no manifest at all, including relatives travelling with a Dravon informant who knew nothing of the arrangement. Ysara Sorn's patrol-map knowledge is what makes the Crooked Landing survivable, and Dravon wants it back.

Internal split: Saevik prices passage by his own moral arithmetic and never confirms which route signs are his; Neyra Vey puts passengers over cargo every time and tells the true version of her licence story least often; Brannoc refuses only carelessness; Ysara gives selected warnings to the Unbroken Accord and refuses both thanks and membership, so the crew's quiet debts to the Archive are hers and not the Halo's.

In play: The load at the False Manifest Desk bound for buyers in Quilrath's outer rings with a manifest that says something else (quest "Corridor — The Manifest That Lies"); the Bent Halo legitimate-parts counter at Grit and Supply, which Saevik depends on Veyra Corsair for; and Jessa Quorin's route sightings, traded from the Rooftop Lookout Walk.

A player can: fly a run with Neyra through the Concealed Departure Cut and owe Saevik a favour he names later; carry the false manifest and become the name on it if the paper fails at a Kathvar checkpoint; or ask Brannoc who sat on the Refugee Bench without being on the count, which he answers once and remembers.

The Black Pennant.name: The Black Pennant
The Black Pennant.basicInfo:
The Black Pennant — Dustfall.

A displaced-house gang built around survivors and descendants of House Vaereth.

The Black Pennant preserves house identity, trains displaced youth, shelters refugees, recruits angry survivors, and uses coercion when belonging becomes indistinguishable from ownership.

No organization here rules Dustfall.

Leader: Rhex Vaereth, commander of the Black Pennant. Reputation: protective of Vaereth refugees, dangerous to everyone else, and a name that makes every Vaereth audit in Quilrath worse.
The Black Pennant.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: A share of the Pennant's income is raiding framed as restitution, and Rhex Vaereth has gone further against defectors than anyone outside Selka Vaereth knows. Torven Vaereth softens enforcement orders in the execution; Eyla Marris treats the Pennant's enemies in secret and would again; Selka keeps a contingency for the day Rhex goes too far, and she is the only reason the band is not yet openly suicidal.

Internal split: Rhex treats leaving as betrayal and does not accept a defector's surrender; Selka would trade the banner for the members' lives and can never say so; the young respect Torven over Rhex; Kalen Dorr knows which refugees are wavering toward which crew before any leader does, and Corren Nhalor keeps interrupting his recruitments.

In play: The family-association review of the Vaereth name moving through the Standing Office in the Gray Rings toward Pennant business in the south, which neither Sedran Vaereth in the Ashrings nor Rhex knows about; Selka's deals with the Unbroken Accord that neither side fully trusts; the Locked Recruitment Chamber and the Old House Archive in the Old Banner Hall.

A player can: help a young Vaereth leave through Selka's Agreement Room and make an enemy of Rhex, who anchors rather than pursues; bring Sedran's audit to Selka before it lands, at the cost of telling the Pennant that Quilrath still holds Vaereths; or take Pennant shelter and learn that the name comes with the enforcement.

The Last Line Company.name: The Last Line Company
The Last Line Company.basicInfo:
The Last Line Company — Dustfall.

A respected local mercenary company based near the perimeter.

The Last Line is reliable, expensive, and willing to break a contract when the work becomes indefensible. That moral line creates trust and enemies in equal measure.

No organization here rules Dustfall.

Leader: Tavra Korrin, captain of the Last Line Company. Reputation: reliable, expensive, protective of civilians, and known to walk off a paid job; trust and enemies in equal measure.
The Last Line Company.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The refusal list is longer than the inventory because Brask Hollan flags the emotionally wrong jobs over food long before Tavra Korrin makes the refusal official; the moral line the town admires is a kitchen habit. Maela Drin sets casualty priorities in the field on her own authority and discounts the frightened, and she is not certain her answer about a mercenary company differs from Eyla Marris's about a gang.

Internal split: Tavra coordinates with Draxen Sol without accepting his authority; Joric Pell will not sell routes to bounty crews and shares route observations with Ysara Sorn without trusting her; Brask is welcome at the Dustfall Meal Yard and the Nhalor Rooms, which makes him the company's one unguarded door.

In play: The escort Tavra dropped at the Contract Table on learning the client meant to raid refugee housing, with the client now hiring at Claim Camp and the Nhalor Rooms and the Old Banner Hall in reach (quest "Dustfall — The Contract Tavra Dropped"); Joric's route memo, which moves Veyra Corsair's supply counter at Grit and Supply.

A player can: take the other side of the dropped contract and stand at the Refugee Approach Lane against Ravik Rusk's crew, paid in Last Line trust and nothing else; buy a route memo off Joric's Route Deck and learn what a patrol change means before it is announced; or ask Maela how she orders the wounded, and be counted in her answer.

The Claimants.name: The Claimants
The Claimants.basicInfo:
The Claimants — Dustfall.

A transient bounty and contract crew based at Claim Camp near the North Routehead.

They bring outside warrants, money, intelligence, and arguments about which authorities Dustfall should recognize.

No organization here rules Dustfall.

Leader: Ravik Rusk, negotiator of the Claimants. Reputation: legalistic, effective and unwelcome in residential streets; tolerated while they obey local boundaries.
The Claimants.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Miren Tal thinks she is selling arrival data; the Dravon intermediary who buys it is buying people, and her sold records have already surfaced in a Nivarek escapee-classification file, so the Accord's southern door leaks through Claim Camp. Ravik Rusk is testing how hard Dustfall will defend Sennra Sol's refusal of Dravon-only warrants, one posting at a time.

Internal split: Ravik treats a clean surrender as undamaged inventory; Cyrra Hale will not fake a finding and has started letting targets hiding among refugees slow her down; Dask Ren has begun questioning Miren's records and does not know what he does when one fails; Miren can make a name check out or quietly fail to, and only she knows which she did last.

In play: The valid Dravon-aligned warrant on the Warrant Board (event "The Warrant Dustfall Refuses"), argued at the Dispute Table of The Long Shot; the arrival record in Miren's Record Module that contradicts Ovar Kethrin's list in the Last Names Room (quest "Corridor — The Name on the Wrong List"); the client Tavra Korrin dropped, now under Ravik's Negotiation Awning.

A player can: bring Dask the record that fails and split the crew, at the price of a bounty posted on someone the player has met; sell Miren a name and learn later who paid for it; or stand with Sennra at the Dispute Table and become the face Ravik posts next.

The Unbroken Accord.name: The Unbroken Accord
The Unbroken Accord.basicInfo:
The Unbroken Accord is Quilrath’s resistance: one name over two wings in permanent tension. The Archive preserves the names and histories that Dravon erases and helps people escape. The Edge sabotages classification infrastructure and attacks checkpoints and auditors. Both wings are the Accord; neither controls the other. Cells maintain mutual deniability, with no central leader. Dustfall itself is not part of the Accord, and receiving aid or selling supplies does not confer membership.

Leader: none; see basicInfo. Reputation: in the rings, a rumour kept for the deep Ashrings; in Dustfall, help some support, some profit from, and some fear will bring Dravon down on the town.
The Unbroken Accord.hiddenInfo:
The resistance is one name over two wings in permanent tension:

### The Archive

The Accord's founding wing, and the reason for its name: it keeps unbroken what Dravon breaks. Hidden cells — their keepers called **Binders** — maintain the true registry: real names, conquered-house histories, grade-audit falsifications, and the lists of the disappeared and the Erased. The Archive forges standing documents, runs escape lines south, and holds one article of faith: *Dravon breaks houses. Names hold.*

### The Edge

The wing the Archive never wanted: sabotage of classification infrastructure, checkpoint ambushes, and retribution against auditors. Small, hunted, and convinced that a library never freed anyone. Every Edge operation brings reprisal audits down on the rings — which is the Archive's standing argument against it, and the argument has no clean winner. Both wings are the Accord; neither controls the other.

### Structure and reach

- Cells with mutual deniability; no central leader; captured cells cannot unravel the whole.
- **The Quiet Mile** — a stretch of the Southreach where the patrol schedule has been quietly purchasable for years — carries the escape lines to the Accord's **Dustfall-facing outpost**, the settlement the Dustfall master references. Dustfall itself remains NOT Accord, exactly as its canon locks state; the mutual-aid lists run through the outpost, not the town.
- The Archive suspects it has a friend inside Nivarek's record system. It does not know who. (Part I's Myrra Nivarek seed remains deliberately unconfirmed — do not resolve it.)
- Ovar Kethrin's Dustfall memorial lists and the Archive's registry of the Erased are two ends of the same thread.

The outpost is a mixed support settlement with a small permanent continuity core, including families, and a larger rotating population of route crews, scouts, couriers, traders, refugees and other guests. Its continuing functions include food preparation, sleeping space, storage, repair, local communication and a basic care room with trained responsibility. Rotating relief and specialist help support ordinary care, stabilization and recovery; supplies and referrals limit what can be treated. ADR-0042 develops these support functions into eight internal areas and local arrangements in The Handoff, the outpost’s local nickname rather than a formal faction institution. Receiving help or selling supplies does not confer Accord membership.

The settlement uses repurposed infrastructure with locally added shelter and support. Its deeper original builder and date remain unconfirmed. No central Accord leader, headquarters or sovereign corridor territory follows from its permanent population. The Archive–Edge disagreement remains unresolved, including the risk that an operation brings reprisals onto residents and escape lines.

House Castro.name: House Castro
House Castro.basicInfo:
House Castro represents freedom, choice, personal sovereignty, protection, restraint, responsibility, strength without conquest, and power used only when necessary.

They are considered one of the truest heroic houses on Nexara. Their defining idea is not that they are weak or passive, but that they are strong enough to refuse domination.

House Castro does not police. House Castro protects.

Castro is the ideological opposite of Dravon:

- Dravon: Strength should create order.
- Castro: Strength should protect freedom.

Castro power is stabilizing, protective, socially trusted, and restrained. It should never feel like authoritarian disarmament, royal decree, or divine rule.

House Castro is not royalty. Avoid the following framing unless a future canon change explicitly asks for it:

- King
- Queen
- Prince
- Princess
- Throne
- Crown
- Royal bloodline
- Divine right
- Royal house
- Monarchy framing

Castro's present political dominance comes from historical power, reputation, cultural prestige, restraint, and the stabilizing weight created by Darkstar's personal control of the Relstaris Core. The Core is not hereditary Castro property, and this influence does not make the family royal.

Leader: Darkstar Castro, head of House Castro; he holds the Relstaris Core as a separate position. Reputation: the truest heroic house on Nexara, trusted for what it refuses to take.
House Castro.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The house's senior members privately share the old terraces' worry that the peace rests on Darkstar Castro personally. Lucera Castro has written contingency notes on it; Sevran Castro spends his influence making it untrue; Vega Castro builds civic trust that would survive his brother; Darkstar himself cannot answer whether he restored the balance or became the only thing holding it.

Internal split: Darkstar spends his own standing keeping the Core and the Castro seat visibly separate, and Lucan Castro refuses to spend his access the way anyone expects; Caivan Castro's peace with losing the Core is unfinished in one sparring match the two have never held; Nina Castro breaks the house's quiet and the family would prefer her quieter.

In play: The Public Aid Office case Lucan cannot carry himself while Cassor Dravon calls Castro aid patronage in the Republic Council Chamber (quest "House Castro — The Offer That Can Be Refused"); Lucera's contingency notes in the Protected Family Archives of the Castro Citadel; the visitor shadowing Selene Castro through the Starfall Promenade (quest "Solvraxis — Counting on No One Armed").

A player can: carry the offer that can be refused and find out what a household in Low Relstaris does with a Castro debt; read Lucera's notes and hold a thing the house would rather nobody outside held; or ask Darkstar the terraces' question to his face and get the one answer he does not have.

House Genesis.name: House Genesis
House Genesis.basicInfo:
House Genesis is the second most powerful major house on Nexara. It represents overwhelming physical power, storm-like combat presence, directness, instinct, endurance, challenge-driven pride, loyalty, and blunt humor.

Genesis does not rule Korrvane through terror. They rule because nobody seriously believes they can be removed, and because the city remains functional under their authority.

### Ark Genesis

Ark is Korrvane’s mythic gravity. His strength makes Genesis rule feel physically unquestionable, but he does not manage daily administration. His presence anchors the city’s challenge culture and gives the Arena its impossible upper limit.

### Tacitus Genesis

Tacitus is Korrvane’s operational ruler. He manages infrastructure, disputes, gate relationships, tournament administration, minor-house politics, and the daily problems Ark never notices. Korrvane works because Tacitus treats governance as seriously as combat strategy.

### Aela Castro

Aela provides an important social contrast inside Genesis territory. She cannot fight by meaningful Starian standards, but she is not treated as insignificant. Her intelligence, humor, emotional steadiness, Castro ties, and marriage to Ark demonstrate that Korrvane can recognize forms of strength outside combat even when its instincts favor visible power.

The complete Genesis family roster is consolidated in Part II of this bundle.

Leader: Ark Genesis, head of House Genesis; Tacitus Genesis runs Korrvane day to day. Reputation: unremovable rather than feared; the impossible top of every ladder.
House Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Kaldor Dravon is building a civic crisis designed to provoke the challenge Ark Genesis most wants to make, and Ark's straightforwardness is the mechanism. Tacitus Genesis knows Caelthorn's valid rule readings threaten the ladder more than cheating would, because the ladder is a civic asset only while it is administered honestly; Corvinus Genesis keeps private notes on how every family member, Ark included, could be beaten.

Internal split: Ark wants an honest fight and someone who comes back after losing; Tacitus governs the city Ark does not notice; Sorvina Genesis watches tournament crowds for Dravon observers and has never been wrong; Valerius Genesis prepares the capitol's protection force for a succession contest he shares with no politician; Norvina Genesis has looked at leaving the city more than once.

In play: Tacitus's plain no to Caelthorn and Zelvaris over the House Seating Tiers, to be carried into Giscara's Reception Hall and the reply brought back exactly as spoken (quest "House Genesis — Word for Word"); Ark's friendly Core challenge at the Core Challenge Court (event "The Friendly Challenge"); the Old Training Markers on Genesis Ridge, which Orvanus Genesis alone can read.

A player can: carry the ruling word for word and be the one Giscara Caelthorn insults by name; point Sorvina at a spectator and be right, or wrong, in front of the House Seating Tiers; or ask Orvanus about the markers and be given advice instead of an answer, daily.

House Contair.name: House Contair
House Contair.basicInfo:
House Contair does not believe power should come from ancestry, command, or raw force.

Contair believes power comes from understanding a problem deeply enough to make it stop being a problem.

Core values:

- competence
- preparation
- independence
- revision
- redundancy
- evidence
- maintenance
- practical creativity
- personal responsibility
- refusal to remain vulnerable
- improvement through failure
- systems that protect people without demanding obedience

The philosophical contrast with House Dravon is direct:

> Dravon: Strength should impose order.

> Contair: A good system should make imposed order unnecessary.

The danger inside Contair thinking is overprotection. A system built to remove fear can still shape every decision. Vexorath's best internal stories come from the line between safety and control.

Leader: Rezulith Contair, head of House Contair. Reputation: officially outside house politics and practically indispensable; every gate on Nexara answers to its standards.
House Contair.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Overprotection is built into the city's systems, and the line between safety and control is being tested by the house's own people. Lumina Major has refused Rezulith Contair records Rezulith considered operational; Talris Contair has found unauthorised routing in the Relstaris Core and must ask Rezulith for help without letting Vexorath take the capitol's heart; Solanis Contair holds deep-space traffic patterns that fit no known route and announces nothing.

Internal split: Rezulith builds for a technically grounded argument and will not pay delay; Seris Contair and Lumina Minor build alternatives instead of arguing; Maelis Contair treats indirect privacy leakage as unfinished work; Drexan Contair keeps failure as evidence; Tavris Contair keeps Echo work off every stage; Mira Contair once stranded emergency supplies with a closure.

In play: Paul Thovex's challenge in the Privacy Challenge Chamber (quest "Vexorath — More Than Intended"); the Outer Shell layer that woke for a threat category nobody remembers creating (quest "Vexorath — The Layer That Woke"); the shared-court workaround in the Modular Family Rows (quest "House Contair — The Way It Is Actually Used").

A player can: learn the workaround from residents and hand Maelis a fault with no name on it, or with one; go into the Repair Crawl Network for Tavris and be the hands when the layer decides; or carry Talris's problem to Rezulith and decide afterwards which city the Core answers to.

House Corsair.name: House Corsair
House Corsair.basicInfo:
House Corsair is built around three old branches:

1. Magic
2. Commerce
3. Swordsmanship

These branches are archaic compared to more modern Starian institutions, but they remain central to Corsair identity.

### Magic Branch

The Magic Branch preserves Corsair’s unusual magical traditions and maintains close ties to The Open Circle in Helvyra. Magic is legal and visible in Helvyra, but most Starians still have not heavily adopted it. They often view it with curiosity or confusion rather than hatred.

Corsair values magic because it can be useful.

The craft's rules — what learned magic is, its costs, and how it relates to Starian affinity and the Elyri — are governed by `canon/core/16_Magic_and_Affinity_Framework.md`.

### Commerce Branch

The Commerce Branch controls trade routes, Waypoints, shipment disputes, markets, alcohol trade, cargo systems, and much of Helvyra’s public-facing economy.

This was once the branch led by Xyren’s father. After his death, Xyren inherited Commerce as well as his Magic Branch responsibilities.

### Swordsmanship Branch

The Swordsmanship Branch is overseen by Rux Corsair and preserves the leading sword style on Nexara. It gives House Corsair serious martial credibility and keeps the family from being dismissed as only merchants, magic oddities, and trade opportunists.

Xyren Corsair is the current head of House Corsair, carrying Magic and Commerce responsibilities. Rux Corsair heads Swordsmanship. The Open Circle is independent of the House; ties and guests do not confer ownership.

Leader: Xyren Corsair, head of House Corsair; Rux Corsair heads Swordsmanship. Reputation: the planet's movement and trade, joked about through Xyren's signs because it matters.
House Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Xyren Corsair carries Commerce he never trained for, and the missing-cargo dispute the city calls theft is, in Sereth Varriko's assembling record, insurance fraud from inside the trade network itself. Tavik Corsair knows what actually moves against what is declared; Rux Corsair would be alarmed by word of someone blending Veltrax pressure into Corsair movement, because it means the style is leaking or someone inside is freelancing.

Internal split: Commerce (Xyren, Tavik, Tavren Corsair, Veyra Corsair) counts numbers that will not reconcile; Swordsmanship (Rux, Vaelor Corsair, Seryn Corsair, Korriven Corsair) argues whether the sign tradition is marketing or corrosion; Magic (Maelrix Corsair, Myris Corsair) keeps catalogues the other branches cannot read; Arven Corsair will not undercut Xyren for anyone.

In play: The consignment two cases short at the Skyhook Docks with three branch explanations (quest "House Corsair — Three Branches, One Answer"); the shipment that never reached Grit and Supply (quest "Dust On The Route"); Korriven's record of which ambushes felt staged; the Legacy Chamber for Xyren's father at the Corsair Estate, where the Helvyra Gate Compact's obligations sit.

A player can: give Xyren one answer and make two branches wrong in front of him; carry Korriven's road evidence to Sereth and turn a family matter into a Varriko finding; or trade on the Route Board Gallery against Tavren's reroute nobody ordered and find who ordered it.

House Volen.name: House Volen
House Volen.basicInfo:
House Volen leads Ignivex, a geothermal fortress-city whose locally maintained systems support substantial independence. Its culture values endurance, territorial pride, family loyalty, direct expression and refusal to kneel to Dravon. Advanced geothermal infrastructure, dangerous home-ground fighters and defensible terrain support its survival. Dravon applies raids, border strikes, sabotage and political intimidation, but has not committed to a full invasion. Volen intensity is communal and expressive; it is not Dravon’s imposed hierarchy. The House can hold major territory without becoming politically expansionist.

Leader: Cynar Volen, head of House Volen. Reputation: the flame that would not kneel; admired for holding Ignivex, watched for what grief may make Cynar do.
House Volen.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Soren Dravon's name is a lever Dravon agents almost certainly already hold, and Cynar Volen suspects it and refuses to admit it. Tharen Volen is designing failure modes to make a captured geothermal network worthless and has told no one; Iskara Volen may know the real reason Dravon wants Ignivex and has found nobody ready to carry it.

Internal split: Cynar closes on the word negotiation; Varessa Volen plans around the day someone uses Soren's name to pull him out of position; Tyra Volen has backed an authoritarian rival's proposal in the Republic because it was the only effective one; Oryn Volen cannot back down publicly without feeling his mother's killers win twice; Selyra Volen's disputes arrive too conveniently and she has not decided whether her ledger arms Cynar or inflames him.

In play: The pressure fault in the Heat Tunnels beside one of Tharen's Sabotage Watch Points (quest "Ignivex — Heat Below the Streets"); the watchpoint beyond the walls Varessa needs held through a heat cycle (quest "House Volen — Through the Heat"); the casualty figures read at the Record Desk of the Smoke Court (event "The Court After the Raid").

A player can: hold Varessa's watchpoint and report what moved rather than what was feared, and be the face no Dravon scout has yet; bring Tharen's fault to Cynar as sabotage or as worn metal, and own the consequence either way; or say Soren's name in the Emberward and watch who else reacts.

House Dravon.name: House Dravon
House Dravon.basicInfo:
House Dravon rules Quilrath through control, pressure, discipline and imposed hierarchy. Its polished Inner Circle presents black star-glass towers, state ceremony, elite comfort and silent classification systems, while suffering is pushed outward and hidden through records and controlled movement. Kaldor Dravon remains active, fully in command and dangerous; he delegates daily operations deliberately while planning the longer game. Sorin is the visible blade and Vaelen the cold strategist, both under succession pressure. Their ambitions do not mean Kaldor has abdicated. House membership does not confer Kaldor’s individual affinity or remove personal motives and dissent.

Leader: Kaldor Dravon, head of House Dravon. Reputation: the primary destabilizing force on Nexara; twice beaten, never dismantled, and planning a third war.
House Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Records that should exist in the Red Ledger do not, and Kaldor Dravon treats it as a front to be mapped before it is fought, without knowing whom the mapping will implicate. The succession contest between Sorin Dravon and Vaelen Dravon is itself the test, with no passing grade, and Serak Dravon and Irala Dravon are being measured the same way; Kaldor keeps Soren Dravon visible as bait; Maelra Dravon keeps a second set of notes, a crime she wrote the definition of.

Internal split: Sorin wants recognition and cannot be sold patience; Vaelen wants a third war fought by someone who does not believe the gallery; Cassor Dravon's lawful-participation project in Relstaris ends the day Dravon hands are found in a civic failure; Orvane Dravon audits the machine and has never asked what he does when it points at a Dravon.

In play: The Inner Compliance Gate's processing record that no longer matches what the Civic Watch Plazas report (quest "House Dravon — Walk the Gates Unknown"), to be reported back to Orvane in the Red War Room; Kaldor's War Gallery, whose captions Maelra's sources contradict; the Quiet Defection Room in the Dravon Compound.

A player can: walk in unclassified for Orvane and become a record the Inner Compliance Gate now holds; read Maelra's second notes and carry a truth the regime defines as crime; or answer one of Kaldor's tests well enough to be measured for usefulness, which he rewards instantly and forgets slowly.

House Myralis.name: House Myralis
House Myralis.basicInfo:
House Myralis is a medical lineage defined by the belief that survival is not the same as recovery.

The house specializes in:

- trauma medicine
- emergency response
- regenerative treatment
- neural recovery
- affinity-related injury
- prosthetics
- artificial organs
- mobility support
- long-term adaptation
- patient consent
- clinical ethics
- biological and synthetic-system integration

House Myralis does not hold major territory or compete for dominance. Its influence comes from being trusted with cases other houses cannot safely solve.

Myralis is a minor house politically and a major institution medically.

## 2. Cultural Principle

> A treatment is not successful merely because the body survives it.

Myralis judges medicine through five connected questions:

1. Did the patient survive?
2. Did the treatment preserve identity and agency?
3. Can the patient live with the outcome?
4. Can the treatment be maintained without permanent coercive dependence?
5. Was consent meaningful under the circumstances?

This philosophy creates natural tension with House Contair.

Contair often asks whether something can be built.

Myralis asks what living with it will cost.

## 3. Place in Vexorath

House Myralis settled permanently in Vexorath because Contair technology created medical possibilities that required an independent clinical authority.

The alliance is based on mutual limits:

- Contair provides fabrication, diagnostics, adaptive systems, artificial organs, prosthetics, and infrastructure.
- Myralis controls medical judgment, patient consent, recovery protocols, and clinical ethics.
- Neither house may unilaterally convert the other's field into a subordinate service.

House Myralis is not a Contair vassal.

The Myralis Continuum is integrated into Vexorath's systems but maintains independent patient records, medical review procedures, and refusal authority.

Leader: Avara Myralis, head of House Myralis. Reputation: the physicians who take the cases others refuse, and whose refusals powerful houses must explain around.
House Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The veto that keeps the Continuum independent is spent on an argument the house means to keep alive: Avara Myralis and Torren Myralis disagree on how long a physician may wait, and the day a patient is lost on either side of it, the alliance's medical veto is what gets questioned. Selvara Myralis has repaired tissue responding to affinity it was never designed to support; Ivera Myralis has paused, unpublished, a recovery method that works and alters affinity behaviour.

Internal split: Torren intervenes and debriefs honestly; Caelor Myralis will not certify a discharge; Neris Myralis files engineering that makes its wearer a subscriber as a flaw; Ilyan Myralis reports ground truth upward whether or not it is welcome; Evara Myralis and Caelia Myralis hold the Myralis Capitol Clinic's independence on their own spines.

In play: The resident of the Modular Family Rows who chose the slower treatment and stopped answering Ilyan (quest "House Myralis — What Living With It Costs"); Aelis Myralis's clinic records in Low Relstaris, which could solve crimes she will never surrender; Ivera's paused data at the Medical Research Institute; the Clinical Ethics Chamber.

A player can: be the non-Myralis in the room when the patient is asked what they want, and carry the answer the assistive unit did not; resupply Aelis and earn a loyalty she cannot police; or bring Ivera a case that forces her finding into the open, which makes her famous or finished.

Starian Republic.name: Starian Republic
Starian Republic.basicInfo:
Darkstar Castro created the Starian Republic after taking the Relstaris Core. It governs the capitol’s civic affairs and provides a negotiated framework for shared planetary and external matters. Its council includes the Core Holder and separate seats for Castro, Genesis, Dravon, Contair, Corsair and Volen; each House chooses its own representative. The Core Holder and Castro’s seat are distinct. Darkstar retains final authority over the Core and may act in emergencies, while representatives exercise real influence. The Republic has no automatic domestic authority over the other cities or House territories, including Dustfall. Collective declarations depend on participation and negotiation. Minor Houses participate through representative chambers, petitions, professional bodies and public pressure without each holding a permanent seat; the system remains weighted toward the major Houses.

Leader: Darkstar Castro, Core Holder, forms the capitol government; each major House seats its own representative. Reputation: Nexara's closest thing to a shared voice, weighted toward the largest Houses.
Starian Republic.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Nobody inside the Citadel can prove the machinery beneath Darkstar Castro is protecting the city rather than learning to protect itself. Maris Othrel may find no author at all, only aligned incentives; Cassara Veylen cannot prove to herself that she does not read Darkstar's silence as approval; Kaelis Morven's own archives may hold a challenge that was never honestly registered; Brenn Ordan and Daelor Ravello have found that Thallax Sol governed far longer than official history admits.

Internal split: Oris Taland has never bent procedure once; Cassara will sign a cruel policy to avoid a citywide one; Mireva Sol keeps files that make symbolic access politically expensive; Elyra Varriko is hunting whoever altered a treaty and no faction fully protects her; Cassor Dravon calls Castro aid patronage on the record.

In play: The Republic Council Chamber during Ark Genesis's friendly Core challenge, when a session stops mattering (event "The Friendly Challenge"); the Treaty and Contact Archive in the Starian Republic Forum, where Elyra's altered clause sits; the Minor-House Petition Office, where hundreds of houses queue for seats they do not have.

A player can: bring Maris a name for the pattern and be wrong in a way that costs an advisor; carry a petition through the Minor-House Petition Office and learn what Oris's calendar does to the powerless; or witness a challenge at the Core Challenge Court and be one of the people Kaelis must verify.

Relstaris Academy.name: Relstaris Academy
Relstaris Academy.basicInfo:
Relstaris Academy is the most prestigious educational institution on Nexara.

It is not only a combat academy.

It trains the planet's future:

- Fighters.
- Researchers.
- Physicians.
- Engineers.
- Teachers.
- Administrators.
- Diplomats.
- Historians.
- Artists.
- Performers.
- Merchants.
- Chefs.
- Public protectors.
- Legal specialists.
- Trainers.
- Magical practitioners and comparative magic scholars.
- Designers.
- Civic workers.
- Professionals in fields that may not yet have names.

The Academy's prestige comes from access to:

- Cross-house expertise.
- Famous instructors.
- Rare facilities.
- Planetwide competition.
- Professional recruitment.
- Public recognition.
- Research partnerships.
- Alumni influence.
- Opportunities unavailable in most home cities.

The Academy is chartered under the Republic but is not controlled as a direct office of the Citadel. Its internal leadership, faculty, review systems, and professional schools possess substantial independence.

Every major house attempts to influence it.

No major house fully controls it.

### Academy Admissions Principle

The Academy accepts students from every recognized house and from independent or disputed backgrounds when they meet its standards or secure an approved path.

Applicants may enter through:

- Direct examination.
- House sponsorship.
- Civic scholarship.
- Professional recommendation.
- Competitive placement.
- Transfer from another institution.
- Exceptional public achievement.

Access is formally open, but wealth, preparation, family reputation, sponsorship, and political pressure still affect who arrives ready to succeed.

### Academy Story Principle

> Nexara sends people to Relstaris Academy to become exceptional. The Academy forces them to decide what exceptional means beside everyone else.

Its breadth and political prestige do not make it best in every discipline. Specialist institutions retain superiority in their own traditions. Studying a tradition here does not automatically grant protected House mastery. Tuition and support vary by program and actual circumstances.

Leader: Caelir Thalen, Rector of Relstaris Academy. Reputation: the most prestigious institution on Nexara; every major house tries to own it, none does.
Relstaris Academy.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The rector protects the Academy's reputation before confronting the harm inside it, and knows it. Caelir Thalen negotiates when the Academy is threatened and resists when a student is; Tessa Sol's scholarship was funded for political reasons, and she is right; Sevra Quorin holds a finding both academic traditions would rather co-opt than concede and has not announced it.

Internal split: Neraya Orvessa makes admissions exceptions with loud authors waiting for one to fail; Syla Volen's success quietly indicts Aurex Genesis's doctrine; Saren Valcoro teaches confidence instead of obedience and sponsors keep trying to buy it out of him; Velis Dravon is the test case for whether a Dravon can be lawful here; Maren Orvessa has buried information that would have ruined students who fixed their own mistakes.

In play: The prodigy defeat in the Public Challenge Ring with something wrong nobody can name (event "The Prodigy Defeat"); Nexis Contair's field study that cannot get past Dessa Sol's door (quest "Study — Readings from the Flooded Foundation"); Auria Genesis's architecture portfolio hidden among her training notes; the Lost Sponsorship Office.

A player can: get consent in Low Relstaris for Nexis and be the reason a study happens, or the reason it does not; find the irregularity in the prodigy's bout before the student news does and choose who hears it; or ask Neraya for an approved path and become the exception her critics are waiting on.

The Open Circle.name: The Open Circle
The Open Circle.basicInfo:
The Open Circle is Helvyra’s independent institution for learned magic, teaching, certification and restricted archives. Its standards support honest charms and ward-marks on Waypoint cargo. Lecturers, students, certification applicants and working charm-writers use it; magic remains a visible minority craft rather than a universal Helvyran ability. First Lecturer Quenna Sil guards its independence from House Corsair. Maelrix Corsair is a resident bridge to the Estate, and Corsair members are guests rather than owners. Students undertake lectures, testing and paid piecework. Certification can be refused, and institutional ties do not waive real training or professional standards.

Leader: Quenna Sil, First Lecturer of the Open Circle. Reputation: Helvyra's home of learned magic, respected for its marks and watched for how close it sits to House Corsair.
The Open Circle.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: A confiscated student route-charm worked where route-charms cannot, Quenna Sil has failed to reproduce it every time, and anyone who identifies its maker before she understands it can force her hand. Maelrix Corsair keeps an exact account of everyone who mocked the craft until they needed it; Myris Corsair catalogues artefacts reacting to affinities neither discipline explains.

Internal split: Quenna refuses endowments, residences and every reasonable Corsair proposal because that is exactly how an academy becomes a house asset; Maelrix is the Estate's bridge and a guest, and the family reads his residence on the island as a foothold; the piecework students at the Charm Piecework Edge need Corsair coin and Circle marks both.

In play: The charm sold from the Charm Piecework Edge carrying a certification mark the Certification Hall has no record of issuing, which works (quest "Study — The Hand Behind the Mark"); the Restricted Archives, where the confiscated route-charm sits; Verel Ondin's forged seal at the Common Scale Hall (event "The Forged Seal"), the same question in another trade.

A player can: trace the mark for Quenna and choose whether the maker's name reaches her, Corsair's magic branch or the market; carry a piece of the route-charm problem to Myris's annex and hand the Circle's mystery to the Academy; or take uncertified piecework for a good reason and be the student caught doing it.

House Valcoro.name: House Valcoro
House Valcoro.basicInfo:
House Valcoro is one of Solvraxis’s four locked Castro-derived minor Houses. The four are peaceful and are not at war with each other.

Castro-style combat discipline, university, civic defense training, movement education, non-weapon defense, and restraint under pressure.

Valcoro supports academy life, training arcs, student comedy, non-lethal defense, and ethical use of strength.

Leader: Marcon Valcoro, head of house and senior master of the protection curriculum. Reputation: the certification other cities respect; control before force.
House Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Marcon Valcoro builds civic defence capacity as though the Castro peace might one day have to stand without its keystone, and gave Marea Valcoro her first student group a year early to watch what she does with the fear. Ilaria Valcoro fears certified restraint becoming a habit of fear wearing good manners; hospitality-as-screening works because Solvraxis has never been seriously tested, and Neressa Valcoro knows it.

Internal split: Marcon will not inflate a score; Ilaria certifies who may teach the public form and argues by letter with her Relstaris kin Saren Valcoro about where control ends and fear of power begins; Lioren Valcoro reads readiness in a child and no pressure accelerates him; Tavian Valcoro's slate shows patterns he cannot place; Mariel Valcoro watches the Castro Compound's own staff.

In play: The arrival Calessa Orvessa flagged who is shadowing Selene Castro and counting on the fact that no one is armed (quest "Solvraxis — Counting on No One Armed"); the blade flagged at the Civic Peace Stations (event "The Blade at the Peace Line"); Marea's lesson plan; the Sealed Training Garden.

A player can: help Neressa answer the visitor without a weapon and learn whether the screening holds; sit Marcon's certification and fail with a perfect score; or read Tavian's slate with him and find whose afternoons keep clearing at the same hour, which is a thing the academy will not want known.

House Ravello.name: House Ravello
House Ravello.basicInfo:
House Ravello is one of Solvraxis’s four locked Castro-derived minor Houses. The four are peaceful and are not at war with each other.

Archives, Starian history, lineage records, cultural memory, public history, and record integrity.

Ravello supports mystery, history, identity, family records, altered documents, and slow-burn political memory without making Solvraxis a conspiracy city by default.

Leader: Maereth Ravello, head archivist of the Ravello Archive House. Reputation: Solvraxis's living memory; trusted with records, suspected of deciding when they open.
House Ravello.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Maereth Ravello's letters with Daelor Ravello in Relstaris are in effect negotiating when Nexara may remember the era before Darkstar Castro's rise. The refusals in Eloria Ravello's ledger thin around the years before the present peace; Veylan Ravello's off-catalog shelf holds restored pieces naming people who afterwards vanish from the record, and Maereth has chosen never to inspect it; Sovian Ravello has found a lineage entry he certified that may be wrong and touches a family of real standing.

Internal split: Maereth releases memory at a survivable pace; Eloria wants records opened one case at a time and keeps the receipts partly as ammunition; Nessa Ravello finds what the catalogue denies and Maereth has never seen her whole list; Caleon Ravello has never asked his marriage to open vaults; Maris Ravello's oversight board runs on data curated by the people it reviews.

In play: The old house agreement Nessa found referenced in a lineage entry Sovian swears is exact, whose document the catalogue says does not exist (quest "Study — The Agreement Nobody Can Find"); Veylan's shelf in the Sealed Record Vaults; Daelor's unpublished evidence at the Living Archive.

A player can: do the tracing with Nessa so the finding is the archive's, and become a reader with a page in it; learn which page Sovian keeps re-reading and hold the registry's one soft spot; or carry a letter between Maereth and Daelor, and read it.

House Bellovari.name: House Bellovari
House Bellovari.basicInfo:
House Bellovari is one of Solvraxis’s four locked Castro-derived minor Houses. The four are peaceful and are not at war with each other.

Markets, arts, public culture, civic beauty, pubs, festivals, music, gallery life, artisans, and social warmth.

Bellovari supports slice-of-life play, public rumors, market errands, cultural events, comedy, and the idea that peace must be lived.

Leader: Viaro Bellovari, head of house and steward of the market district. Reputation: the warmth Solvraxis runs on; hospitality that decides more than the council knows.
House Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Viaro Bellovari knows exactly how many days of grace Solvraxis has if the Corsair routes falter and has said the number to no one. Seressa Bellovari keeps private records correlating cultural programming with civic mood, and her calendar is civic policy disguised as entertainment; Darian Bellovari's nightmare is the day a courier he likes brings in the crate he watches for.

Internal split: The Solvraxis line and Arissa Bellovari's Relstaris branch keep a three-generation argument over who left whom; Liora Bellovari decides a great deal by choosing what to repeat and never discusses the Castros; Nerova Bellovari has not learned that information cannot be un-sold; Serrin Bellovari's market placement in Relstaris rests on a curated ignorance about which stalls survive on which arrangements; Alessa Bellovari resists the sponsors a hostile audit could paint her as captured by.

In play: The reunion Arissa has not answered (quest "Solvraxis — Who Left Whom"); the season's star-glass from the Star-Glass Workshop that needs both branches to agree (quest "Trade — Star-Glass for the Hundred-House Market"); the Silver Cup Pub; Viaro's unspoken number.

A player can: negotiate the star-glass as someone neither branch can call the other's, and be owed by both; get Viaro's number out of him and become the second person who knows it; or feed Liora a rumour and watch it travel with her credibility attached.

House Orvessa.name: House Orvessa
House Orvessa.basicInfo:
House Orvessa is one of Solvraxis’s four locked Castro-derived minor Houses. The four are peaceful and are not at war with each other.

Civilian welfare, shelters, healing support, guest care, family protection, counseling, public trust, and school life.

Orvessa supports recovery, care work, emotional scenes, student support, guest orientation, and the haven identity of Solvraxis.

Leader: Amara Orvessa, head of house and director of the welfare district. Reputation: the reason Solvraxis is safe enough to study in, visit and raise families in.
House Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Amara Orvessa built the welfare district to survive the day the haven reputation is finally tested and cannot say so without weakening the belief she protects. Jovian Orvessa keeps the district's real reserves in his head and files welfare notes as supply notes; Renzo Orvessa silently backstops his runs and would deny it under oath; Ceyra Orvessa knows where every vulnerable family in Relstaris sleeps, in a system only she reads.

Internal split: Amara remembers exactly who arrived late; Calessa Orvessa's memory of first impressions is the district's most sensitive record; Elia Orvessa trusts first and verifies second, and her sisters are the cost; Mirae Orvessa's schoolroom is the district's listening post; Neraya Orvessa's admissions exceptions at the Academy have loud authors; Maren Orvessa keeps protecting the wrong-to-protect anyway.

In play: The Emergency Shelter Supply Room reconciled against Renzo's ledgers before certification, with Jovian made to hand over the count (quest "Solvraxis — The Reserve Count"); Calessa's flag on the arrival shadowing Selene Castro; Ceyra's file of where families sleep, kept in the Public Welfare Administration.

A player can: help Jovian give up the count and learn what the reserves were really for; be routed by Calessa to what they truly need and find out afterwards what she wrote down; or ask Ceyra for a family's location for a good reason and be refused, which she does for a person's own good regardless.

House Veyth.name: House Veyth
House Veyth.basicInfo:
House Veyth is a small, faded minor House of notaries, record-keepers and appraisers, seated in Solvraxis. It is not Castro-derived, and its presence does not change the four locked Castro-derived minor houses above, which remain exactly four. Head of house: Malkor Veyth; seven members.

Its standing is thin — no district, no civic seat, and no political weight beyond the authority of its seals — and it holds no governmental authority, no ministry and no access level. Its player-facing presence in the city is `The Veyth Notary`, an area of the main Solvraxis location (§27).

House Veyth is not House Vey, the unrelated Dustfall flight-service family; the two are separate and neither is evidence for the other.

Leader: Malkor Veyth, head of House Veyth. Reputation: thin standing, real seals; the Notary whose witness nobody can impeach, in a house few people notice.
House Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The Veyth archive holds an old contract worth a fortune to destroy and ruin to expose; which family it touches and what it proves stays unanswered. Malkor Veyth will neither sell nor burn it, and his brother Edran Veyth has already asked a broker what suppressing it might fetch; two ceremonial seal casings Malkor handles weekly are plated copies Thessa Veyth substituted; Oren Veyth is secretly duplicating the archive to protect it, betraying its first principle.

Internal split: Malkor treats the archive's integrity as the entire substance of the house; Edran frames self-interest as prudence; Liora Veyth has twice been outbid trying to buy back an inflated valuation carrying her signature; Meris Veyth copies for a rival office under a false name and wonders which career is real; Caevin Veyth let the satchel out of his hands for one night three years ago and never reported the gap.

In play: The Veyth Notary in Solvraxis, where bonded weapon storage receipts pass (event "The Blade at the Peace Line"); the old contract itself; Oren's cache; the broker who now knows a Veyth asked.

A player can: bond a blade through the Veyth Notary and hold a receipt nobody can impeach; find Oren's cache and choose whether Malkor learns of it; or learn which family the contract touches and become the person that family pays or removes, without ever learning what the contract proves.

House Orvantis.name: House Orvantis
House Orvantis.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Orvantis Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Old Fading House  
🏷️ Reputation: Ancient, dignified, past its peak  
❓ Core Question: What remains when glory fades but dignity does not?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Weathered bronze-black, ivory, old stone, preserved honor markers

House Orvantis has been in Korrvane longer than most houses can clearly trace. Its decline was gradual rather than catastrophic. The house continues to compete every week, carries losses with discipline, and behaves as though public dignity remains a form of power.

Some residents admire that endurance. Others believe Orvantis is trapped by its own memory.

Leader: Hannovar Orvantis, house leader. Reputation: see above; ancient, dignified, past its peak, and still in the bracket every week.
House Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Kelvan Orvantis's fall is the one loss Hannovar Orvantis considers his house took incorrectly and has never publicly acknowledged; Kelvan now fights debt matches in the Hollow Ring in Relstaris, where fixers pay to injure prodigies. Bostarix Orvantis has never told Hannovar how close the house's district standing came to slipping.

Internal split: Hannovar answers every argument by appearing in the bracket; Vaelris Orvantis admits the failures plainly and cannot prove whether an old precedent is preserved as he remembers it; Sophira Orvantis and Melqara Orvantis both want the house to become something new and neither has said so where Hannovar can hear; Hasdrovex Orvantis fears Sophira is right and keeps it under his likability.

In play: Hasdrovex's injuries at the Recovery Yards that do not match his public bout, and Bostarix's protest that the Betting Stands, the Zelvaris Recovery Annex and Baalrix Caelthorn all have reasons to shape (quest "Korrvane — Wounds That Don't Match"); Hamilqa Vorreth's records, which may preserve the Orvantis precedent differently; Kelvan in the Fighter Holding Rooms (event "The Clean Exit").

A player can: work the registry review and find who shaped the injury, at the cost of one house's goodwill; put Vaelris's precedent against Hamilqa's record and settle a thing the house has idealised; or buy Kelvan's clean exit and learn what he never left for.

House Zelvaris.name: House Zelvaris
House Zelvaris.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Zelvaris Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Hungry Challengers  
🏷️ Reputation: Closest minor house to meaningfully pressuring the Genesis ladder  
❓ Core Question: How much can discipline close an impossible gap before ambition becomes self-destruction?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Dark teal, charcoal, metrics, reinforced training architecture

House Zelvaris has built its identity around measurable improvement. It has not defeated Genesis, but it has come close enough to force the city to watch carefully.

Zelvaris treats losses as information. This creates admirable discipline, dangerous pressure, and a culture where rest can feel like failure.

Leader: Barcavon Zelvaris, house leader. Reputation: see above; the hungry challengers who treat every loss as data and rest as failure.
House Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Barcavon Zelvaris's near-victory is a ceiling he cannot iterate past, and every rebuilt methodology is an argument with one night he will not discuss. Tannivar Zelvaris holds a complete unpublished file on Alcandrus Genesis, and his models break on Bomivex Vorreth in a way that has stopped being professional; Varek Zelvaris's ledger at the Hollow Ring connects respectable patrons to illegal violence.

Internal split: Barcavon cannot be persuaded to wait; Eshmunar Zelvaris overprotects and hides what the old injuries still cost him daily; Magara Zelvaris is terrified of the bracket moving one week without her and rest offered as advice enrages her; Hamilvar Zelvaris keeps a tactical map of every contender, housemates included; Abdesara Zelvaris studies Hamilvar's patience rather than the doctrine she quotes.

In play: Tannivar's Alcandrus file in the Combat Data Archive; the Zelvaris Recovery Annex named in Bostarix Orvantis's protest (quest "Korrvane — Wounds That Don't Match"); Varek's sold match and the Clean Exit Program (event "The Clean Exit"); Kaedra Vossan, one incident from forcing Cavren's question open in Dustfall.

A player can: get Tannivar's file before a Genesis Ladder attempt and owe a house that measures debts in improvement; make Magara rest and become the person she blames for the week; or take Varek's depreciation schedule and be entered in the ledger that is life insurance and death warrant both.

House Caelthorn.name: House Caelthorn
House Caelthorn.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Caelthorn Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Rule-Edge Manipulators  
🏷️ Reputation: Always technically within the rules; universally mistrusted  
❓ Core Question: Is a fair system still fair when one house understands it better than everyone else?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Polished black, ivory, silver, controlled asymmetry

House Caelthorn does not describe itself as dishonest. Its members find exact boundaries, exploit allowances, control wording, and weaponize social expectations.

The tournament has reviewed Caelthorn methods repeatedly. The house remains eligible. This frustrates everyone more than a clear conviction would.

Leader: Giscara Caelthorn, house leader. Reputation: see above; never convicted, never trusted, always eligible.
House Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The eligibility reviews keep failing only because Giscara Caelthorn has never once needed to cheat, and she treats the house's rare real innocence as the one asset she will not spend. Sophavel Caelthorn's discomfort with the method is monitored by Giscara the way other leaders monitor injuries, and Tanithra Caelthorn has not decided whether to protect or use it; officials have opened a file on Magozra Caelthorn, which would thrill him if he knew.

Internal split: Baalrix Caelthorn drafts language that outlives the match and will not misstate a rule to win; Adherix Caelthorn keeps a private list of those who beat him clean, unlitigated; Tanithra collects favours at most once; Korrik Caelthorn in Dustfall certifies performance nobody else will, and his customers' injuries reach the Frontier Care House with his modifications attached.

In play: Tacitus Genesis's plain no over the House Seating Tiers, to be carried into Giscara's Reception Hall (quest "House Genesis — Word for Word"); Baalrix's reasons to shape Bostarix Orvantis's protest (quest "Korrvane — Wounds That Don't Match"); Kyren Luxaryn's management agreement with Vara; the Quiet Agreement Rooms.

A player can: bring Giscara the ruling and be offered warmth, access and an alibi in return for something later; give Sophavel one victory she can describe honestly, condition by condition; or find the file on Magozra before he does, and decide whether he gets to be thrilled.

House Aevon.name: House Aevon
House Aevon.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Aevon Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Aerial Fighters  
🏷️ Reputation: Dominant in open sky, predictable on the ground  
❓ Core Question: When the city itself favors your style, is mastery skill or privilege?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Blue, white, bronze, aerodynamic shapes, open air

House Aevon turned Korrvane’s vertical design into a complete combat and social identity. Its members understand altitude, descent, wake pressure, traffic flow, and aerial positioning better than any other minor house.

Their pride is justified in open sky and vulnerable whenever opponents force them onto the ground.

Leader: Bomilvar Aevon, house leader. Reputation: see above; masters of the open sky, ordinary the moment they touch the ground.
House Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Bomilvar Aevon has drilled grounded scenarios exactly twice, alone, and told no one what he found. Magonex Aevon holds a complete counter-file on Elissara Aevon that he built defensively and dreads ever winning with; Elissara's joints have started whispering about the form and she avoids the recovery benches; Hannoq Aevon takes secret pre-dawn ground lessons from Magonex.

Internal split: Bomilvar breaks off rather than fight at an altitude he did not choose and has declined to solve Elissara's succession problem; Gisqon Aevon's judgment lane is treated as binding regardless of the rules; Yadira Aevon privately ranks her courier network above the gates; in Relstaris, Yara Aevon's ledger of the elite at their worst and Yven Aevon's logs of everything above the capitol have never been bought.

In play: The transit corridor that failed in the Flight Lanes during tournament traffic, with Gisqon insisting someone used the lane incorrectly and Genesis suspecting sabotage (quest "Korrvane — The Lane Failure"); Elissara's Speed Run; the Non-Flier Waiting Lift everyone associates with Hannoq; Corvinus Genesis's invitations to Bomilvar.

A player can: read the lane failure with Yadira's couriers and name a cause Gisqon or Genesis will not like; force an Aevon to the ground in a bracket match and find out whether Bomilvar's two drills were enough; or keep Hannoq's dawn sessions secret and be owed by a house that never frames anything as a disclosure.

House Luxaryn.name: House Luxaryn
House Luxaryn.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Luxaryn Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Party House  
🏷️ Reputation: Average combat record, unmatched social influence  
❓ Core Question: Can hospitality become political power in a city obsessed with fighting?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Wine-red, bronze, cream, food, music, warm light

House Luxaryn hosts Korrvane after the fighting ends. Its feasts, food routes, music, guest lists, and open doors create relationships that better-performing houses often lack.

Luxaryn proves that reputation is built through who feeds the city, who keeps rivals speaking, and who creates a place to return after public failure.

Leader: Hadavar Luxaryn, house leader. Reputation: see above; the house that feeds Korrvane after the fighting and is owed by everyone it fed.
House Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Milkon Luxaryn means to convert the house's informal warmth into explicit political leverage, which would spend in a season what took generations to grow, and Hadavar Luxaryn has not decided how to stop him. Qartessa Luxaryn runs the most complete informal intelligence network in Korrvane and deploys it almost entirely as soup; Salambor Luxaryn keeps a short absolute exclusion list whose subjects believe scheduling has simply never favoured them.

Internal split: Hadavar competes because appearing matters and yields cheerfully; Didobara Luxaryn has drafted an alternate competing identity and never filed it; Hannix Luxaryn's losses hurt exactly as long as pouring the first round; Milkon's ledger keeps getting corrupted by actual friendship; Hessan Luxaryn cannot say whether he means to teach Rin Sol or own her; Kyren Luxaryn is only beginning to map the cost of Vara Caelthorn's management agreement.

In play: Hadavar's Feast Hall after any weekly final, where the after-match gathering becomes the city's real political centre; Milkon's ranked map of social debts; Salambor's list; Tessik's Booth at Black Dust, where unbilled decencies fit no pricing model Tessik Luxaryn will admit to.

A player can: eat Qartessa's soup and learn what the Betting Stands do not know yet, in exchange for being someone she can ask later; read Milkon's map and be placed on it; or be excluded by Salambor and never learn why, until Hannix pours the round that tells them.

House Vorreth.name: House Vorreth
House Vorreth.basicInfo:
📍 District Location: Vorreth Quarter  
🏷️ Archetype: The Wildcard  
🏷️ Reputation: Impossible to model consistently  
❓ Core Question: What happens to a culture of public measurement when one house refuses to produce a stable pattern?  
🎨 Visual Lane: Muted plum, gray, black, bronze, controlled asymmetry

House Vorreth is not new or unknown. It has competed in Korrvane for years, yet its tactics, records, public roster, and results resist confident interpretation.

Vorreth should feel mysterious without becoming supernatural horror, shadow magic, or random nonsense. The house may be strategic, private, culturally unusual, or deliberately anti-predictive. Canon should not settle the question too quickly.

Leader: Azrubara Vorreth, house leader. Reputation: see above; the house nobody in Korrvane can model, and nobody has caught cheating.
House Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Whether the house's unreadability is strategy, culture or something else is unsettled inside the house itself, and what Bomqara Vorreth is for is a question only Azrubara Vorreth appears able to answer. Azrubara lets contradictory theories circulate because prediction itself can be exploited; Hamilqa Vorreth's records have never been proven wrong nor right, and may preserve an Orvantis precedent Vaelris Orvantis remembers differently. Canon does not settle the question, and the narrator should not either.

Internal split: Hamilqa controls information through records and Sufeta Vorreth through language; Bomivex Vorreth answers everything honestly and explains nothing, and buys the beaten analyst a drink; Magovar Vorreth carries two results she declines to expand or explain; Bomqara trades worse questions for any certainty offered about her.

In play: Bomivex's Record Wall against the Arena's public records, which disagree about who competed in an earlier round; Magovar's next match, the most-watched non-final in bracket memory; Tannivar Zelvaris's and Hamilvar Zelvaris's models, which break on Bomivex; the Guest Room That Was Not There Yesterday.

A player can: fight a Vorreth and be the data that breaks a rival's model, which Zelvaris will pay for and Vorreth will not thank; compare Hamilqa's record with Vaelris's memory and settle one precedent while unsettling a house; or accept the guest room and be asked, later, what was there.

House Varriko.name: House Varriko
House Varriko.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: trade law, cargo insurance, warehousing, contract enforcement  
City Role: commerce rival and legal pressure house  
Relationship to Corsair: dependent rival  
Primary District: Varriko Ledger District  
Secondary Area: Varriko Bond Vaults

House Varriko is one of Helvyra’s strongest commerce-focused minor houses. They do not move goods better than Corsair, and they do not control the Waypoint network, but they specialize in the legal and financial systems that make large-scale trade trustworthy.

If Corsair moves the cargo, Varriko often knows who insured it, who owns it, who is lying about it, and who will pay when it disappears.

Varriko members are polished, legalistic, and extremely difficult to intimidate. They rarely raise their voices because they believe a properly written clause can do more damage than a threat.

House Varriko is not villainous by default. They protect merchants from fraud, punish careless shippers, and make contracts mean something. The problem is that they also know how to weaponize paperwork.

## Culture

House Varriko values precision, memory, reputation, and controlled leverage.

They admire people who can win a dispute without a fight. They consider theft barbaric, bad accounting unforgivable, and verbal promises charming but worthless unless backed by witness, seal, or collateral.

Their family saying is:

“If it mattered, someone signed for it.”

Leader: Sereth Varriko, head of House Varriko. Reputation: exact, unbluffable and quietly feared; if it mattered, someone signed for it.
House Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The corruption is inside the process. Dren Varriko holds three genuine, mutually impossible records for one shipment; Oren Varriko has found a sealed bond replaced with a perfect fake, and the list of people capable of it is the list he would report it to; Sereth Varriko believes the missing-cargo dispute the city calls theft is insurance fraud from inside the trade network. Mavriel Varriko's policy terms sometimes price a threat she has no admitted way of knowing about.

Internal split: Sereth wants a finding, not sympathy; Dren wants numbers that match and house pride buys nothing; Oren refuses the collateral to anyone, calmly; Calia Varriko in Relstaris memorises what she cannot afford to file and suspects someone counts her delays; Miri Varriko is an archive of private dinners she has never sold.

In play: The three signed records at the Ledger Court Annex that must reach the Varriko Ledger Hall as a finding before Sereth calls it fraud (quest "Helvyra — Three Signed Records"); Oren's fake in the Varriko Bond Vaults; Mavriel's insurance offer on the inventor's run (quest "Trade — Running the Lot to Helvyra"); Verel Ondin's forged seal (event "The Forged Seal"), possibly the same hand.

A player can: carry Dren's audit to the Hall and be the witness a Varriko clause names; find the forger Verel needs found without the finding becoming public, and hold what Oren cannot report; or sign Mavriel's terms and learn what she knew about the route.

House Yalven.name: House Yalven
House Yalven.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: manufacturing, weapon modifications, armor fittings, support-model assembly  
City Role: Forge Rows power house  
Relationship to Corsair: contracted partner with quality-control tension  
Primary District: Yalven Forgeworks  
Secondary Area: The Support Model Line

House Yalven is a manufacturing minor house rooted in Helvyra’s Forge Rows. They are not as innovative as Contair, not as militarized as Dravon, and not as prestigious as the old major houses, but they are practical, fast, adaptable, and everywhere.

Yalven makes the things people actually buy.

Weapon mods, armor fittings, courier gear, replacement plates, support frames, cargo clamps, custom handles, repair kits, aftermarket parts, and older licensed support models all pass through Yalven facilities.

Contair only permits older support models to be manufactured outside Vexorath under strict oversight, and House Yalven is one of the few Helvyra families trusted enough to handle that work.

One bad production scandal could damage their house for years.

## Culture

House Yalven values craft, speed, practical durability, and customer feedback.

They believe a thing is not truly tested until it has been used by a courier who did not read the manual, a swordsman who refuses to maintain it properly, or a Dustfall buyer who needed it to work yesterday.

Their family saying is:

“Pretty breaks first. Useful comes home.”

Leader: Torvane Yalven, head of House Yalven. Reputation: the things people actually buy; one production scandal from years of damage.
House Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: A faulty batch has surfaced that Torvane Yalven believes was sabotaged and cannot prove, and if the Contair inspectors reach their own conclusion first they close the Support Model Line, the house's crown and its throat. Kesh Yalven's best mod matches a restricted pattern stolen from a Dravon contractor; Nera Yalven has narrowed a buried design change to three people with access, and one of the names makes no sense.

Internal split: Torvane will take a bad deal to protect the floor before a good one that costs jobs; Nera documents to protect the house by refusing to flatter it; Fenra Yalven is sitting on armour damage from a shipment attack that points to a sword school; Kesh asks far too few questions; Pell Yalven saw someone enter the Restricted Contract Floor after hours and cannot admit where he was.

In play: The sabotage proof Torvane needs before the inspection cycle closes; Fenra's dented plate, which Daxor Veltrax's blade-wear reading and Rux Corsair's alarm both bear on; Kesh's Dravon-pattern mod in the Weapon Adjustment Bays; the Open Circle's piecework charms failing on the same day, which Yalven wrongly blames on a materials fault.

A player can: prove the sabotage for Torvane and be owed by a house that pays in useful things, or fail and watch the line close; get Pell to say where he was and hold the night that names the third person; or ask Fenra which school her plate points to and carry that across the river to whichever hall it indicts.

House Veltrax.name: House Veltrax
House Veltrax.basicInfo:
House Type: minor house  
Primary Role: rival sword art, aggressive dueling, martial prestige  
City Role: swordsmanship rival to Rux Corsair’s school  
Relationship to Corsair: open martial rival, not enemy  
Primary District: Veltrax Redcourt District  
Secondary Area: The Pressure Hall

House Veltrax is Helvyra’s most visible rival sword-art house. They do not possess the number one sword style on Nexara, but they are skilled, proud, loud, and talented enough to make themselves impossible to ignore.

Veltrax swordsmanship is aggressive where Corsair swordsmanship is adaptive. Corsair blade work emphasizes movement, timing, route-reading, and turning conditions into advantage. Veltrax teaches pressure, pursuit, forced exchanges, and breaking an opponent’s rhythm before they can escape into clever movement.

Veltrax is not villainous. They are a genuine martial house with real skill, pride, and frustration at living in a city where Rux Corsair’s school dominates the blade conversation.

## Culture

House Veltrax values courage, pressure, direct challenge, and visible proof of skill.

They believe a swordsman should not wait for perfect conditions. A swordsman should create conditions through force of will and relentless advance.

Their family saying is:

“Forward is also a defense.”

Leader: Arvessa Veltrax, head of House Veltrax. Reputation: Helvyra's loud second blade; skilled, proud, and tired of the city saying only one school's name.
House Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Kaelen Veltrax believes the impossible standard breaking his students is a fake seeded into his hall by someone, and would work with the rival school to expose it rather than lose one more shoulder. Daxor Veltrax reads from blade wear that someone is blending Veltrax pressure with Corsair movement; Meya Orlin at the Bankside Care Hall sees a wound pattern matching no known style, progressing from crude to clean; Sava Veltrax is quietly redesigning what the house is for.

Internal split: Arvessa Veltrax's exhibition invitation to Rux Corsair's students is a trap she considers fair and will not fix; Mireth Veltrax has not reckoned with what follows a public match against Seryn Corsair, win or lose; Sava routes escort contracts to prove a point and keeps it commercial; Kaelen and Daxor hold a diagnosis neither school can get elsewhere.

In play: Sava's escort contract out of the Hauler Yards built to prove Veltrax guards outperform Corsair route defenders, with Korriven Corsair put on the same convoy (quest "Helvyra — The Escort Proof"); the Pressure Hall, where the fake standard lives; Meya's open ledger of the pattern; Fenra Yalven's dented plate.

A player can: ride the escort proof and be the witness both houses cite; bring Kaelen and Rux into the same room over the blended style, at the price of being the one who said the style leaks; or fight Mireth on the Public Challenge Floor and give her the thing she has not reckoned with.

House Nivarek.name: House Nivarek
House Nivarek.basicInfo:
House Nivarek serves Dravon’s legal-memory system in Quilrath. It records loyalty, classifies conquered families, audits citizens, enforces oaths, manages accusations and makes obedience procedural. Its records and standing authority are distinct from Kathvar’s ordinary administration and Balrath’s physical infrastructure. Nivarek makes conquest permanent by recording it; precision, silence and procedural pressure define its public presence.

Leader: Thamur Nivarek, head of House Nivarek. Reputation: precise, silent and feared; the house that makes conquest permanent by writing it down.
House Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Records are vanishing from Red Ledger Prime, the house's own sealed archive; Kaless Nivarek's access logs show nothing, and he has told no one, including his brother Thamur Nivarek, while quietly watching Myrra Nivarek, Maelra Dravon and Orvane Dravon. Whether Myrra is the Archive's friend inside or merely fits the hole is genuinely unresolved and stays so; Ferrik Nivarek keeps illegal duplicates of his own audits, with a grade he falsified years ago among them.

Internal split: Thamur considers House Dravon a client civilisation that has not noticed; Ruvena Nivarek administers standing as a genuine believer; Oryn Nivarek's courtesy is exactly what the forgers exploit; Vessa Nivarek's sealed transcripts fail to exist downstream; Elyra Nivarek would be owned by anyone offering honesty without treason.

In play: The Correction Archive and Red Ledger Prime in the Nivarek Compound; the reprisal list published after classification infrastructure burns at a Standing Office (event "The Accord Argues With Itself"), which lands on Ferrik's office; the Vaereth family-association review moving toward Sedran Vaereth; Kaless's arrangement that his death surfaces questions.

A player can: bring Kaless a pattern in what disappears and be handed the last uncorrupted index in the empire for an answer, never for the archive; sit through Vessa's one extra question and learn what it serves; or carry Ferrik's duplicates out of the Gray Rings and hold the fuse.

House Balrath.name: House Balrath
House Balrath.basicInfo:
House Balrath operates Quilrath’s military infrastructure and engineering apparatus. Its Bastion Barracks houses state engineers, wall technicians, gate operators, drone-line supervisors, equipment inspectors, infrastructure crews and rapid-response soldiers. It builds and maintains walls, gates, drones, transit locks, issued gear and border systems. This is advanced military-industrial engineering.
