Dravon owns policy and command, Nivarek standing and classification, and Kathvar ordinary outer-ring civil administration; Balrath’s machinery does not erase those distinctions.

Leader: Arduk Balrath, head of House Balrath. Reputation: the hands on the city's locks; ugly, reliable machinery Dravon commands and depends on.
House Balrath.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The override paths and design margins in the Balrath Gateworks appear in no Dravon specification, and Arduk Balrath calls them insurance until someone asks why they exist. Sennar Balrath has engineered delay margins into the lockdown seals as safety and means them as seconds; Namar Balrath's nightly notebooks hold the empire's best unauthorised understanding of enemy gate technology.

Internal split: Arduk trades schedule, capacity and quiet favours, never loyalty; Durvan Balrath believes the third conflict is the second again on his own roadbeds and is in no hurry to finish them; Kavash Balrath has begun mis-shelving components so his son cannot fill them; Lurani Balrath reads the labour-transit manifests as names and nobody has approached her yet; both houses treat Vandrik Dravon as belonging to the other.

In play: Pelna Ostrek's readings that the Quilrath Gate's next failure is its last, which she will hand to anyone but the Prototype Gate Lab (quest "Quilrath — The Gate's Last Failure"); Namar's notebooks; Sennar's seals in the Inner Wall Control Yards when the Curfew Gates come down (event "Curfew at the Gates"); the manifests in the Labor Transit Systems Office.

A player can: bring Pelna's true readings to Namar and decide whether Dravon gets a gate of its own; give Namar one honest peer review and buy him outright; or ask Lurani one careful question per meeting and be the first to approach her, which someone else is watching for.

House Kathvar.name: House Kathvar
House Kathvar.basicInfo:
Standing: Recognized loyalist minor House of Quilrath.
Primary function: Day-to-day civil administration of Quilrath's outer rings.

House Kathvar is one of the principal groups that makes ordinary government
function beyond the Inner Circle. Dravon rules Quilrath; Kathvar is a large part
of the reason the ruling reaches anybody. Where a resident of the Gray Rings or
the Ashrings actually touches the state — a counter, a queue, a permit, a file,
a clinic intake, a checkpoint — a Kathvar administrator is a routine part of
what they meet.

The House is loyal to Dravon rule. It is not a resistance family, not a
conquered line, and not a nest of secret reformers. Its people see hardship,
inefficiency, and human consequence in the system daily, because processing the
system's consequences is the work; seeing that is not opposition and must not be
written as opposition by default.

### What the work is

Kathvar administrators are encountered in:

- civic intake
- work-order processing
- movement and permit processing
- ordinary civil records
- public-service case routing
- provision administration
- clinic and health-service coordination
- education and civil-service training
- staffing and operations dispatch
- procedural auditing
- checkpoint processing
- queue and service management

This work is distributed throughout the outer-ring civic system rather than
concentrated in one seat. No House compound, headquarters, office building,
district, or map placement is established here.

### The separation of powers

Four Houses divide Quilrath's machinery, and the division is the point:

| House | Owns |
|---|---|
| Dravon | Policy and command |
| Nivarek | Standing, loyalty classification, and high-level records |
| Balrath | Physical machinery and military infrastructure |
| Kathvar | Ordinary outer-ring civil administration |

Nivarek decides standing; Kathvar makes standing decisions operational. Kathvar does not determine Civic Standing Grades. No new House compound or map placement is established.

Leader: Jorek Kathvar, head of House Kathvar. Reputation: the counter, the queue and the permit; loyal, competent, and the reason Dravon rule reaches anybody.
House Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The house is loyal and its competence is the regime's most effective instrument; both are true and neither cancels the other. Bralen Kathvar has never answered whether he wants the house at all; Veyra Kathvar tracks things nobody asked her to and has never been wrong that a bad number is a person who did not get seen. Kathvar never decides a Civic Standing Grade; it makes Nivarek's decisions operational, and that is exactly where the margins live.

Internal split: Mirasha Kathvar finds the margin inside the rule at the Curfew Gates; Sora Kathvar cannot let numbers that do not add up go unexamined; Karessa Kathvar sees the whole system and says little; Odrin Kathvar is more at peace as second than he was as heir; Dalan Kathvar has not learned when procedure needs escalation.

In play: Dalan's mishandled movement permit at the Ring Gate, to be carried to Jorek's counter as a corrected file rather than a complaint about a son (quest "Quilrath — The Corrected File"); the family half-through the Curfew Gates (event "Curfew at the Gates"); Torbek Karn's paper at the Provision Hall (quest "Corridor — Into the Outer Rings"); Bralen's Provision Counter closing.

A player can: carry the corrected file and learn what Kathvar honesty costs a son; get a permit through Sora's desk on paper that reads right and become a name in a queue that is watched; or ask Bralen for the thing that does not match and be given it, with no promise about the future.

House Caldris.name: House Caldris
House Caldris.basicInfo:
House Caldris is the loyalist minor House of Ignivex under Volen — the fortress city's defensive backbone. It specialises in defensive infrastructure, emergency response, wall systems, outer patrols and civilian protection, and it supports House Volen completely. Head of house: Davor Caldris, one of Cynar Volen's strongest political supporters.

Its seat is Caldris Wallworks, a family district and defensive-infrastructure district under its own control. It holds no Council seat and no standing above Volen; its weight in Ignivex is practical rather than political, and the city depends on it the way a city depends on a wall.

Caldris is also one of Relstaris's established minor-house cultures, carried into the capitol by members working there. That is a cultural presence, not a second seat.

Leader: Davor Caldris, head of House Caldris. Reputation: the wall that remembers who stood there; no council seat and the city's whole trust.
House Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Davor Caldris has arranged Caldris planning so Ignivex holds through a leadership crisis without a Volen order, loyalty of the deepest kind and readable as its opposite. Maedra Caldris designs against friends as rigorously as enemies and re-keys the deliberate weaknesses in her own gates on a schedule no document holds; Lysa Caldris is pre-positioning supplies along routes that only make sense for something worse than a raid; raids strike where Rava Caldris's evacuation is hardest, as though someone is learning her routes.

Internal split: Davor lets no argument beginning with surrender reach him; Orvak Caldris keeps private files on border contacts shared only partway up his chain, and framing an innocent Meravil would require only that he be shown evidence; Tessan Caldris has noticed small wrong things on his routes; Korran Caldris's children raised between houses are the pressure point an adversary finds.

In play: Varessa Volen's watchpoint beyond the walls, placed by Orvak's patrol with Tessan running the relay (quest "House Volen — Through the Heat"); Ilvara Meravil's displacement count that Lysa's shelters will act on (quest "Ignivex — Rows After the Raid"); Maedra's Gate Workshop; the Defender Memorial Stones.

A player can: hold the line for Varessa and be placed by Orvak, which puts a name in his files; vary a route with Rava and learn whether the raids follow; or show Orvak evidence about a Meravil and find out how little it takes.

House Meravil.name: House Meravil
House Meravil.basicInfo:
House Meravil is the surrender-leaning minor House of Ignivex under Volen, and the only organised bloc in the city arguing against the war. It holds that Ignivex should negotiate surrender, conditional submission, or some form of Dravon oversight before Dravon finds a way to break the city by force. Head of house: Seralyne Meravil, the most visible surrender-leaning voice in Ignivex.

Its seat is Meravil Ash Hall, a family district and civic-administrative quarter under its own control, where it keeps the casualty records, civic continuity planning and daily administration the city runs on.

They are not traitors by default. Their politics come from fear, casualty records, civilian exhaustion, and the fact that Seralyne's son is married to a Dravon. The house does not speak with one voice: her daughter Auralis argues against surrender at the family's own table, every time it is discussed.

Nyssara Dravon lives under Meravil protection but is Dravon-born and is not a member.

Leader: Seralyne Meravil, head of House Meravil. Reputation: the surrender voice; not traitors by default, and never fully trusted while Nyssara Dravon lives under their roof.
House Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: Vennik Meravil is manoeuvring toward something colder than Seralyne Meravil's fear, on channels nobody else in Ignivex has, and what he has implied, to whom, and on whose authority may not be known even to Seralyne. Ilvara Meravil's arithmetic says Ignivex is losing a war it believes it is surviving; Nyssara Dravon has never volunteered what she knows of Dravon, because it would prove her a traitor to one side without proving her loyal to the other.

Internal split: Seralyne answers fury with casualty figures and trades her own reputation for fewer of them; Auralis Meravil argues against surrender at the family's own table, every time; Caevan Meravil does not know his answer if the city demands he choose between it and his wife; Vennik offers channels as contingency rather than conviction.

In play: The count of damaged homes and displaced households from the Ration And Displacement Planning Rooms, which Vennik wants before it is finished (quest "Ignivex — Rows After the Raid"); the casualty figures read at the Record Desk (event "The Court After the Raid"); the Intermediary Corridors; Orvak Caldris's border files.

A player can: carry Ilvara's finished count past Vennik to Lysa Caldris and Cynar Volen, and be the reason the numbers arrive honest; ask Nyssara what she knows and close her completely, or earn the one insider's read on Dravon method in the city; or find what Vennik implied and decide whether Seralyne learns it before Davor Caldris does.

House Thovex.name: House Thovex
House Thovex.basicInfo:
House Thovex is a minor Vexorath house with little political weight. Canon establishes its standing and its people and nothing beyond that: it holds no Council seat, no district and no compound, and no trade, office or collective action is attributed to it. This record deliberately claims no remit it has not been given.

Two members are established. Paul Thovex is Rezulith Contair's partner and Seris Contair's father, and supplies ordinary-user perspective, external procurement contacts, and social friction against Contair certainty. Sela Thovex, of a Relstaris-born partner-house branch, is Contair Compound steward and civilian usability officer; she and Paul are distantly related.

Its presence in both cities is therefore personal rather than institutional. Thovex people are found inside House Contair's world, not at the head of anything of their own.

Leader: none; see basicInfo. Reputation: a name that means little on its own, carried by two people who tell Contair the truth about ordinary use.
House Thovex.hiddenInfo:
Narrator-only truth: The house has no remit and two people who see what Contair cannot. Paul Thovex is positioned to notice when the real supply chain stops matching the Contair model, and is the one person who will tell Rezulith Contair a perfect design makes no sense; Sela Thovex keeps a private list of systems that passed every review and still fail residents, and the list implicates careers.

Internal split: There is no house to split. Paul stands between Rezulith and Seris Contair as the only person in the household still speaking easily to both sides; Sela is dating Talris Contair after beginning as his professional adversary, and mentors Kellan Pelorr, whose sponsors keep structuring offers to end his independence. The two Thovexes are distantly related, and their presence in both cities is personal, not institutional.

In play: Paul's challenge in the Privacy Challenge Chamber over what infrastructure monitoring recorded of his household (quest "Vexorath — More Than Intended"); Lumina Minor's workshop change with Seris behind it (quest "Vexorath — The Other Architecture"); Sela's list in the Contair Compound; Paul's storage pod marked Possible Further Use in Rezulith's Workshop.

A player can: stand with Paul in the chamber and hear what Lumina Major declines to say; read Sela's list and hold the careers on it; or be the person Paul tells first when the supply chain stops matching, which is a thing Rezulith has not yet been told.
